title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Newport News, VA: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Newport News and Peninsula shipbuilding, fabrication and port welders: corporate, online or one-to-one formats.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Newport News, Virginia: Six Days for Peninsula Shipbuilding, Fabrication and Port Welding Inspectors
html:
Newport News is a shipbuilding town before it is anything else. HII's Newport News Shipbuilding, on the James River waterfront, calls itself the largest industrial employer in the Commonwealth of Virginia, with more than 26,000 people building and overhauling nuclear-powered aircraft carriers and submarines. Thousands of those jobs involve striking an arc or checking the result, and the Peninsula around the yard adds heavy equipment manufacturing, a breakbulk port and a steady flow of structural and pipe work. Atlantis NDT offers a six-day (6-day) course that prepares candidates for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination, working through Part A Fundamentals, Part B Practical and Part C Code Application. It is available as corporate delivery at an employer's facility, as online study at your own pace with an instructor answering your questions, or as one-to-one sessions. The American Welding Society administers the examination and issues the certification; Atlantis prepares people for it and does not certify anyone. There is no Atlantis classroom in Newport News. Atlantis has two offices, one in Houston, Texas and one in Hyderabad, India, so Peninsula candidates study online, book one-to-one time or have their employer host the course. To start a conversation, send a Newport News CWI enquiry.

What the six days cover for a Peninsula candidate

The plan follows the structure of the exam rather than any one employer's procedures. The opening two days deal with Fundamentals: the arc processes, AWS terms and definitions, joint geometry, weld and welding symbols, basic metallurgy and heat input, destructive and nondestructive test methods, discontinuity types, inspector math, safety and the responsibilities that come with the job. Day three is practice for Part B, measuring with gauges and reading procedure and qualification records. Day four lives inside the Part C book you intend to sit. Day five is given over to timed practice papers, and day six revisits whatever those papers exposed and walks through exam logistics. The national AWS CWI exam prep page sets out the same outline in more detail, and all three formats use it.

For Newport News candidates the emphasis often shifts slightly. Yard welders tend to know their processes thoroughly but have spent years working to Navy documents instead of AWS books, so the code-navigation day and the welding-symbol drills usually earn the most attention. Candidates from the manufacturing side of the Peninsula sometimes have the reverse profile: comfortable with AWS D1.1 drawings, less sure of metallurgy and heat treatment.

The yard on the James River and the work it creates

Newport News Shipbuilding has spent more than 140 years on over 800 ships for the Navy and commercial owners. Today its work sits in two large streams, carriers and submarines, and both are welding-heavy for years at a time.

Ford-class carriers and carrier overhauls

The yard builds the Gerald R. Ford class, the first new carrier design in decades. The second ship of the class, the future USS John F. Kennedy (CVN 79), left Newport News in late September 2026 after preliminary acceptance by the Navy, with fleet delivery planned for March 2027 according to Navy budget documents reported by USNI News. Later Ford-class hulls follow behind it on the yard's building ways and in its dry docks. Alongside new construction, the yard carries out refueling and complex overhauls of Nimitz-class carriers; in September 2026 the Navy awarded it the overhaul contract for USS Harry S. Truman (CVN 75), a down-to-the-bulkhead refit covering thousands of compartments and tanks that is scheduled to finish by November 2031.

A carrier overhaul is a different inspection environment from new construction. Inspectors deal with existing structure, cut-outs, inserts and repairs in confined compartments, often against tight access windows. New construction, by contrast, means long runs of production welding on modules and units that must fit together precisely. A CWI candidate who has worked both sides of the yard brings a wide experience base to the exam.

Virginia-class and Columbia-class submarines

The submarine work is shared with General Dynamics Electric Boat. In July 2026 HII announced that the two yards had received Navy contract modifications covering nine more Block VI Virginia-class boats and five more Build II Columbia-class boats. Under those awards Newport News is the delivery yard for six of the Virginia-class submarines and builds and delivers six module sections for each Columbia-class boat. Submarine hull and piping work is among the most demanding welding in the country, controlled by Navy fabrication and inspection documents and by the yard's own written procedures.

Where a CWI fits beside Navy requirements

Acceptance criteria on Navy ships come from the Navy's own specifications and technical publications, and the yard qualifies its inspectors to those documents through its internal program. An AWS certification does not replace that qualification, and the exam does not test Navy requirements. So why do yard people sit it? Because the credential belongs to the individual. It travels with you if you leave for a commercial fabricator, a bridge shop, an inspection firm or an owner's quality group, and it shows a general command of welding inspection that a company-specific qualification does not advertise outside the gate. Check with your quality department how, or whether, it relates to your current role before you plan around it.

Beyond the shipyard: other Peninsula employers that weld

The yard dominates, but it is not the only place on the Peninsula where weld quality matters.

  • Liebherr Mining Equipment Newport News. Liebherr has built crawler excavators in Newport News since the 1970s and moved its mining truck production to the city in the mid-1990s, after acquiring the Wiseda truck business; the plant builds the T 264 and T 284 haul trucks. Its article marking thirty years of truck building in the city described a large investment programme, an expanded training department, a two-year apprenticeship and six robotic welding cells. Heavy frames and structures of that kind are typically built to structural welding requirements, so D1.1 knowledge is directly useful.
  • Newport News Marine Terminal. The Port of Virginia's terminal on the James handles roll-on/roll-off and breakbulk cargo such as construction and farm equipment, heavy-lift machinery, metals and military cargo, on a 125-acre site with on-dock rail. Terminal infrastructure, crane rail and the repair of heavy cargo gear all generate structural welding.
  • Supplier and subcontractor shops. Around a yard this size sit pipe shops, machine and fabrication shops, staffing firms and specialty contractors, many of which need one or two people who can run weld inspection to a written requirement.
  • Construction, utilities and government sites. Steel bridges on the Peninsula are welded to AWS D1.5, commercial buildings to D1.1, and military and federal installations across Hampton Roads add their own steel and piping projects.

Across the river, the south side of Hampton Roads carries a separate ship repair economy; candidates working there can read the Norfolk CWI exam prep page, which deals with the repair yards in more depth.

Learning to weld on the Peninsula

Most CWI candidates in Newport News began as welders, shipfitters or pipefitters, and the city has unusually strong routes into those trades.

The Apprentice School

Newport News Shipbuilding's Apprentice School was established on 1 July 1919 and marked its hundredth year in 2019. It is tuition-free, apprentices are paid for their work and their academic classes, and programmes run for several years depending on the trade and on optional advanced tracks. Its welder apprenticeship teaches manual, semiautomatic and automatic processes, preparation checks, weld symbols and preheating, on structural and pipe welds for carrier and submarine construction and overhaul. Shipfitter and pipefitter trades are taught there too. A completed apprenticeship is a well-documented block of welding-related experience, which helps when you list your history on the AWS application.

Virginia Peninsula Community College

The former Thomas Nelson Community College became Virginia Peninsula Community College after the State Board for Community Colleges approved the new name in September 2021. Its non-credit welding training covers stick, flux-cored, MIG and TIG processes and pipe welding, with classes at the Hampton campus in the Peninsula Workforce Development building and at the Toano Trades Center near Williamsburg, plus blueprint reading and an introduction to welding codes. The college describes its Welding Center as an AWS Accredited Testing Facility that runs AWS welder certification tests, so Peninsula welders can earn welder qualifications without leaving the area. Those welder tests are separate from the CWI examination, which AWS runs through its own testing arrangements. Both the Apprentice School and the college are independent of Atlantis.

The AWS section for Newport News

Hampton Roads members are served by the AWS Tidewater Section in District 4. Its recent technical meetings have included an equipment maker's laser welding demonstration and a plasma cutting demonstration held at the VPCC Workforce Development Center in Hampton, which puts section activity within easy reach of Peninsula welders. Section meetings are a good place to talk with practising inspectors, hear which employers are short of qualified people and line up the supervisors who will vouch for your experience. If you are unsure which section covers your address, the section finder on aws.org lists every section and its contacts.

Choosing a Part C book from a Newport News background

Part C is open book, and you take it on one code chosen from the AWS list, which includes AWS D1.1 structural steel, D1.2 aluminum, D1.5 bridges, D15.1 railcars, D17.1 aerospace, API 1104 pipelines, an ASME option combining Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option. There is no Navy option, so a yard candidate answers from one of these books.

Where your experience comes fromCode book to considerReasoning
Hull, deck and foundation welding, shipfitting, structural unitsAWS D1.1The broadest structural steel code, and the book shore-side employers most often name
Ship piping, valves, boiler and propulsion pipingASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3Qualification variables plus piping examination and acceptance rules
Heavy equipment frames and fabricated structuresAWS D1.1Matches the structural requirements most manufacturers work to
Bridges and highway steel on the PeninsulaAWS D1.5The bridge welding code used on transportation projects
Aluminum structures and small craftAWS D1.2Aluminum-specific qualification and inspection

AWS names the edition it uses for each book, and that edition is not always the newest, so buy or borrow the right one before you tab it. Further reading: AWS D1.1, ASME Section IX and AWS D1.5.

Experience, vision and the application

AWS sets the experience requirement by education level: more schooling, including recognised trade or technical training, reduces the years of welding-related work you need, and less schooling increases them. The experience must be verifiable work on welded products, and AWS alone decides whether a given history qualifies. Yard experience counts when it is documented with job titles, dates and people who can confirm it; keep copies of apprenticeship records, qualification cards and performance reviews. AWS also requires every candidate to pass a vision test; its current application materials set out what the eye examination covers, who may perform it and how recent it must be. Every candidate applies to AWS individually and meets those rules personally, whether or not an employer is paying. The CWI requirements guide covers the eligibility table, and candidates short of the experience can look at the AWS Certified Associate Welding Inspector route first.

For the computer-based parts, AWS issues booking details once it accepts an application, and candidates schedule through its testing provider. The practical part is run by AWS at its own examination sites and dates, so check the current AWS listings for sessions in Virginia or nearby states and leave enough margin around yard schedules and overtime. AWS publishes its examination fees on aws.org.

Studying around yard shifts and test milestones

Production at a large shipyard runs on shifts, overtime and milestones, from keel and launch events to sea trials and undocking dates. Candidates who succeed usually settle on a fixed study habit rather than relying on long free weekends that rarely arrive. The online format suits this: material and practice papers are there whenever you open them, an instructor answers questions as they come up, and there are no set class times to miss when a shift changes. Keep the Part C book where you can reach it during breaks and look up the clauses that govern the joints you see that day. For Part B, handle a fillet weld gauge, a bridge cam gauge and a set of calipers on real coupons until the readings come without thinking; the Practical NDT welding workshop simulator is another way to rehearse inspection steps away from the shop floor.

Running the corporate format at a Peninsula facility

For an employer with several people heading for the exam, corporate delivery brings all six days to the company's own site. The practical day uses the company's gauges and real welds, such as test coupons, production samples and cut-outs, so the measuring practice resembles the work the group will later accept or reject. The code day can concentrate on whichever book most of the group has chosen, or divide time between D1.1 and the ASME package when structural and pipe people are mixed. Plan the six days around production peaks; the employer can encourage and support applications, but each candidate files with AWS and books the exam personally.

One-to-one sessions for a single candidate

One-to-one suits a candidate who wants six days aimed squarely at their own gaps: a pipefitter whose code navigation is slow, a structural welder rusty on metallurgy, or a sailor leaving the Navy who wants to turn years of shipboard maintenance into a civilian credential. Sessions take place online or in person at a location agreed when you book, and the pace follows that one person rather than a group.

After the CWI: NDT and inspection paths from Newport News

AWS keeps the CWI current through renewals and a recertification cycle, and inspectors who want to widen their scope add endorsements or work toward the Senior CWI. Many Peninsula inspectors also move into nondestructive testing, because shipbuilding relies on magnetic particle, penetrant and ultrasonic examination of welds. To perform those examinations a technician needs method training and then certification by the employer under its own written practice. Atlantis provides training built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A in VT, MT, PT and UT; see NDT training in Newport News, UT Level 2, MT Level 2 and VT Level 2. The CWI, API 577 and ASNT Level II comparison helps when you are choosing between credentials.

Nearby CWI pages and how to ask for a quote

Candidates elsewhere in the region can read the CWI exam prep pages for Norfolk, Washington, DC and Baltimore.

When you write, say whether the course is for one person or a group and which format suits, give each candidate's schooling and welding background, name the Part C book each intends to choose, and for corporate delivery describe the facility, the gauges and weld samples available and any production dates to plan around. Fees are quoted on request once we know the scope; we reply within one business day. Use the Newport News CWI enquiry form.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Newport News for the CWI course?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Newport News. Atlantis has offices in Houston and Hyderabad, and Peninsula candidates take the six-day course online at their own pace with an instructor answering questions, as one-to-one sessions online or in person at a location agreed when booking, or as a corporate course at their employer's facility. See the course outline.

faq.q: Does Atlantis issue the CWI certification?
faq.a: No. The American Welding Society administers all three parts of the examination and issues the CWI to candidates who pass. What Atlantis provides is exam preparation for Peninsula candidates, and AWS has neither approved nor endorsed that course.

faq.q: I am a shipbuilding apprentice. Does my apprenticeship count toward CWI eligibility?
faq.a: It can. AWS decides what counts, but a documented apprenticeship gives you trade training plus verifiable welding-related work. Keep your records, dates and the names of supervisors who can confirm them, and check the current AWS eligibility table before you apply.

faq.q: Does a CWI replace the Navy qualification I hold at the yard?
faq.a: No. Navy work is inspected to Navy documents, and the yard qualifies its inspectors under its own program. The CWI is a personal credential that is recognised outside the yard and shows general welding inspection knowledge; ask your quality department how the two relate in your role.

faq.q: Which Part C code should a Newport News shipfitter choose?
faq.a: Most structural and shipfitting candidates pick AWS D1.1, because it is the broadest structural steel book and the one shore-side employers ask for. Pipe welders and pipefitters often prefer the ASME option of Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3.

faq.q: Can my employer on the Peninsula host the six days?
faq.a: Yes. In the corporate format the full six days run at the employer's facility, using the company's own gauges and weld samples on the practical day. Each candidate still applies to AWS and books the exam personally.

faq.q: How much does the course cost?
faq.a: Fees are quoted on request because they depend on the format, the number of candidates and, for corporate delivery, the location. AWS publishes its own examination fees on aws.org. Send an enquiry and we reply within one business day.

faq.q: Where do Newport News candidates take the exam?
faq.a: AWS runs the CWI exam: the computer-based parts are booked through its testing provider once your application is accepted, and the practical part is held at AWS examination sites on AWS dates. Check the current AWS listings for sessions in Virginia or nearby states.

faq.q: Is the welder certification test at the community college the same as the CWI exam?
faq.a: No. Welder qualification tests, such as those Virginia Peninsula Community College runs at its Welding Center, test your ability to make a weld. The CWI exam tests your ability to inspect welds and apply a code, and AWS administers it separately.

faq.q: What can I do after passing the CWI?
faq.a: Many inspectors add AWS endorsements or aim for the Senior CWI, and many move into NDT. Atlantis offers SNT-TC-1A-based training in VT, MT, PT and UT; see NDT training in Newport News.
